title: fix(sse): deterministic chunking and framing for SSE partial JSON and token/event ordering
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: Customers and internal smoke tests reported intermittent malformed partial-JSON objects when using SSE streaming through the OpenAI compatibility adapter; root cause analysis traced this to non-deterministic delimiter emission and out-of-order token/event boundaries in the SSE streamer when a payload spanned multiple internal chunks. This PR fixes deterministic chunking and framing to ensure partial JSON fragments and JSON delimiter tokens are emitted in a stable, ordered way across backpressure, reconnect, and retry paths. Changes: 1) Introduces a small finite-state framing layer that normalizes token/event ordering and guarantees that delimiter tokens (e.g., 'event:', 'data:', and OpenAI-style delimiter objects) and partial-json fragments are emitted in the expected sequence even when a single logical generated token sequence is flushed across multiple network writes. 2) Adds a strict delimiter ordering policy to the OpenAI compatibility adapter so callers receive complete JSON fragments before the adapter emits closing delimiters. 3) Adds defensive reassembly logic to the partial-JSON parser to tolerate split UTF-8 sequences and to avoid swallowing trailing braces when chunks are re-ordered under rare scheduler preemption. 4) Adds comprehensive unit and integration tests exercising chunk boundaries, backpressure and reconnect flows; tests include synthetic long-token sequences, multi-byte UTF-8 boundary tests, and a replay of customer-reported reproduction harness. 5) Adds a small metric (streaming.partial_json_reassemblies) to surface reassembly counts for future monitoring. Testing and validation: ran full unit suite and integration streaming tests on linux-amd64 and linux-arm64, reproduced previous failure modes locally and validated the fix. The CI run had an initial flaky integration test which was rerun and passed; no performance regressions observed in p99 latency within measurement noise. Rollout and compatibility: no API contract changes; adapter remains backwards compatible for existing OpenAI-style consumers. Feature gated the new framing layer behind a server-side feature flag to allow fast rollback if needed. Related: closes ENG-3189 and reduces noise for SUP-542. Checklist: [x] Reproduced bug locally [x] Implemented deterministic framing and reassembly [x] Added unit and integration tests [x] Added metric and docs note [x] CI green and PR approval.
